_meta.indication: Adbry is indicated for the treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in adult patients whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable; can be used with or without topical corticosteroids.

pivotal_trials.population: Adults (≥18 years) with moderate-to-severe AD, candidates for systemic therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: IGA 0/1 at Week 16; Secondary: EASI-75 at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 at Week 16: 16% tralokinumab vs 7% placebo; difference 9% (95% CI 4%, 13%), P=0.0017. EASI-75: 25% vs 13%; difference 12% (95% CI 7%, 18%), P<0.001

pivotal_trials.population: Adults (≥18 years) with moderate-to-severe AD, candidates for systemic therapy (same as ECZTRA-1)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: IGA 0/1 at Week 16; Secondary: EASI-75 at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 at Week 16: 21% tralokinumab vs 9% placebo; difference 12% (95% CI 7%, 17%), P<0.001. EASI-75: 33% vs 10%; difference 22% (95% CI 17%, 28%), P<0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Placebo-controlled, double-blind, 2:1 randomized 32-week trial of tralokinumab in combination with topical corticosteroids (TCS)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults (≥18 years) with moderate-to-severe AD, candidates for systemic therapy (same as ECZTRA-1, -2)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: IGA 0/1 at Week 16; Secondary: EASI-75 at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 at Week 16: 38% tralokinumab+TCS vs 27% placebo+TCS; difference 11% (95% CI 1%, 21%), P=0.033. EASI-75: 56% vs 37%; difference 20% (95% CI 9%, 30%), P<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): upper respiratory tract infections (23.8% vs 20.4% placebo), conjunctivitis (7.5% vs 3.1%), injection site reactions (7.4% vs 4.1%), and eosinophilia (1.4% vs 0.5%). Warnings include hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis and angioedema) and conjunctivitis/keratitis.
target_moa: Human IgG4 monoclonal antibody that specifically binds to interleukin-13 (IL-13) and inhibits its interaction with the IL-13 receptor α1 and α2 subunits, neutralizing IL-13 bioactivity; an IL-13 antagonist.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting was not held because no unexpected significant safety/efficacy issue or controversial issue was identified.

basis.text: The application was designated standard (not priority) review.

summary.text: BLA 761180 was submitted under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act and reviewed as a standard application. The initial submission (received 4/27/2020) received a Complete Response (4/23/2021) due to insufficient needle-safety device information; the applicant resubmitted 7/2/2021 and Adbry was approved without accelerated approval, breakthrough, orphan, or priority-review designations.
